ai_summary: Great Britain's electricity system is currently operating with a total GB wind output of 3.2 GW, with an estimated Scottish wind output of 1.7 GW, representing 16.8% of installed Scottish wind capacity. Operational decarbonisation highlights a stark regional divergence, as Scottish carbon intensity stands at 0 gCO2/kWh versus 215 gCO2/kWh GB-wide. However, acute cross-border transmission limits prevent this low-carbon power from reaching southern demand centres. As a direct consequence, Scottish generation curtailed so far today has reached 5,359 MWh through Balancing Mechanism bids, incurring a constraint cost of about £158,810. To replace this constrained output, fossil generation was dispatched downstream, burning an estimated 1,018,267 m3 of gas and releasing an additional 1,876 tonnes of CO2 into the atmosphere. Annualising today's expenditure yields an estimated total yearly cost of £58 million. When socialised nationally across standard electricity demand, this ongoing constraint volume is estimated to increase everybody's invoice in the UK by approximately £0.20/MWh, demonstrating how grid bottlenecks simultaneously inflate consumer energy bills and compromise wider decarbonisation progress.
